propositions: The epic-close bug screen degrades all per-candidate LLM provider failures (including Bedrock ValidationException) to verdict C ('unrelated'), silently converting systematic outages into no-op safety checks with no aggregate signal.
When max_tokens is raised for a larger model and later re-used for a smaller model, it is never re-clamped to the smaller model's ceiling, causing a 400 ValidationException on the provider.

A completion-verifier run that fails due to LLM provider error currently returns PASS with no attestation instead of blocking the close, requiring operator decision on fail-closed vs fail-open semantics.

The operator has ratified fail-closed: LLMUnavailableError anywhere in the completion-verifier run must propagate and block the close, consistent with the absent-provider path; --force-close remains the escape hatch.

The fix requires re-raising LLMUnavailableError (and subclass LLMConfigError) from both the warm-call and fan-out layers of screen_candidates and from run_screen's advisory shield before the broad except clauses.
